A held snapshot proves kill precedes release, late facts are omitted, and the witness and record report the same wall and command; a completed snapshot proves pre-kill facts are retained. An unselected timeout writes no artifact, and a spawn refusal releases the dormant helper. Supplied child usage and unavailable load remain labelled. A normal neighbour keeps its bytes with no timeout file, proc fixtures show vanished and truncated facts, and a write failure plus failed witness reconciliation retains the deadline verdict after kill. This establishes reporting behavior, not scheduler or proc availability.

sites.after: Claim: An injected drain timeout and an occupied drain-request slot report counters without inventing loss; an acknowledged drain or guard close delivers every record queued before a request arriving after the worker batch ends, including a full queue. A private test-build observer pins the complete-evidence route whose deployed wait is unwindowed; the windowed test-build wait is pinned at its 600-second containment; delivery held behind an event completes after release, while the windowed contrast expires at its injected zero window with records still undelivered. The private route observer pins the windowed test-build wait at its 600-second containment independently of scheduling. The batch-end, full-queue, timeout and unavailable controls remain. The after-drain event observes completion after the original acknowledgement attempt, so a caller timeout starts no second cleanup request. This claim does not witness the complete route's test-build timeout bound or caller naming. The separate overlapping-drains and event-wait-caller controls own their distinct propositions.

sites.after: Claim: A request accepted while an earlier request drains its FIFO prefix is acknowledged before the worker parks, even when that prefix consumes the later request's wake. At the pre-park event the second acknowledgement must already be available by try_recv; restoring the single slot check fails that assertion without awaiting a timeout.
